# `sunAz()` {#fn-sunaz}

[Function index](function-index.html#idx-sunaz)

```{=html}
<p>A solar reference requires the observer position, timestamp, timezone and the part of
the disc that was sighted. Times are parsed using R's civil-time routines and converted
to UT Julian dates. Swiss Ephemeris supplies the topocentric solar position and its
horizontal coordinates using 1013.25 mbar and 15 degrees Celsius. The returned bearing
is measured clockwise from north. Sighting the left or right limb applies a fixed minus
or plus 16 arcminutes in azimuth. Optional altitude is the geometric centre altitude.
</p>
<p>Astronomical positions require Swiss Ephemeris files covering the epoch. We
recommend installing <span class="pkg">swephRdata</span>; see <code>skyscapeR-package</code> for setup.
</p>
```

[The time and limb of the solar reference](fn-reduct-theodolite.qmd).


<details><summary>Implementation arguments, return value and documented modes</summary>

```{=html}
<table><thead><tr><th>Argument</th><th>Formal default</th><th>Behaviour in this interface</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><th scope="row"><code>loc</code></th><td>—</td><td><p>Location, either a <em>skyscapeR.horizon</em> or a vector
containing the latitude, longitude and elevation of location, in this order.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>time</code></th><td>—</td><td><p>String containing the date and time in the following format:
"YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS"</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>timezone</code></th><td>—</td><td><p>Timezone for civil timestamps. Use UTC or a fixed offset for dates before 1900. See <code>time2jd</code> for named zones and offsets.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>limb</code></th><td>—</td><td><p>Measured limb of the sun. Options are <em>left</em>, <em>right</em>.
If missing the center of the sun will be output.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>alt</code></th><td><code>FALSE</code></td><td><p>Logical that triggers output of altitude of the sun at exact time.
Default is FALSE.</p></td></tr></tbody></table><h5>Return value</h5><p>Solar azimuth in degrees clockwise from north, one value per observation. With alt = TRUE, a data frame with columns az and alt is returned. The altitude is geometric and is expressed in degrees.
</p>
```

</details>

**Implementation.** `R/mechanics.R`.
